name: Xpanner X1 Piling R6
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: driving tracker foundation piles
summary: Tracked solar pile driver that combines Everstar's R6 base machine with Xpanner's X1 automation, so one operator with a remote control can let it travel to each GNSS-surveyed point, align, hammer and plumb the pile. Launched in October 2026 for US solar and battery storage sites.

germany.statusNote: No German or EU sales route found. Xpanner (Santa Fe Springs, California) sells or rents the machine with a monthly X1 software subscription and its own field support team; all deployments it names are in the US and Australia.

specs.label: Max. pile length
specs.quote: Handle piles up to 23 ft long, with a maximum driving depth of 15.7 ft.

specs.label: Max. driving depth
specs.conditions: 4.8 m; actual embedment depends on reveal and site
specs.quote: Handle piles up to 23 ft long, with a maximum driving depth of 15.7 ft.

specs.label: Engine power
specs.quote: The system includes a 97 kW (130 hp) engine

specs.label: Hammer impact energy
specs.quote: a high-frequency hydraulic hammer with up to 1,260 J (929 ft.-lb.) of impact energy and three energy settings

specs.label: Guide-rail fine positioning
specs.quote: The guide rail slides 11.8 in. (300 mm) forward and back and 19.7 in. (500 mm) left and right, and the upper body rotates 180 degrees

specs.label: Operators
specs.quote: Supervised by a single operator, the system uses high-precision GNSS and onboard sensors to place each pile accurately

specs.label: Business model
specs.value: machine purchase or rental plus monthly X1 software subscription
specs.quote: Customers purchase (or rent) the X1 Piling robot and then license the automation software on a monthly subscription basis for each active technology.

notes: Arm = pile-driving mast with hydraulic hammer; Everstar R6 crawler base machine.
roughGround set true for open solar-field ground, not a sourced spec.
Records each pile's position, depth and plumb to the Xpanner Connect web dashboard.
Designed to work with Xpanner's X1 Panel Lift for module installation.

evidence.task: Launched for autonomous pile driving on utility-scale solar and BESS sites
evidence.note: Xpanner says its X1 Piling automation (on other pile drivers) has been deployed at more than 60 US sites; no named R6 site yet.
